prompt_text: What is the best Airbnb or short term rental to book in Nashville for a family of four?
answer_verbatim:
I can help you find the best short-term rental — but I’ll need a few details to give a tailored recommendation. Quick questions first:
- What are your travel dates (or a date range)?
- What’s your budget per night (or total)?
- Ages of the two kids?
- Will you have a car / need parking?
- Do you want to be close to downtown attractions (Broadway/ACM/Bridgestone), Opryland, or prefer a quieter neighborhood vibe?
- Any other needs (pets, accessibility, crib/high chair, fenced yard)?

While you answer, here are general recommendations and practical tips so you know what to look for.

What to book (best options for a family of four)
- Entire 2-bedroom (or 3-bedroom) house or apartment — gives space and privacy. Two separate beds or a family room + bedroom works fine.
- Ground-floor or elevator access if you have a stroller or mobility concerns.
- At least one full kitchen, washer/dryer, reliable AC, and free/secure parking.
- Yard or nearby park if the kids need space to run.

Best Nashville neighborhoods for families
- Green Hills / Forest Hills — quiet, safe, easy access to shopping (The Mall at Green Hills), family-friendly restaurants, and good schools.
- West End / Vanderbilt / Midtown — near Centennial Park, Parthenon, walkable restaurants; good for sightseeing and museums.
- 12South — very walkable with boutiques and kid-friendly places; great for a relaxed local vibe.
- Germantown — historic, walkable, close to downtown but calmer than Broadway.
- East Nashville — hip, family-friendly pockets, lots of parks and restaurants (more eclectic).
- Near Opry / Opryland — convenient if your plan centers on Opry or you want to be near the airport.

Must-have filters/amenities to use on Airbnb or VRBO
- Entire place
- 2+ bedrooms (or “sleeps 4” with two beds)
- Washer & dryer, full kitchen, air conditioning
- Free parking (driveway or on-site)
- “Family/kid friendly” or amenities like a crib/pack ’n play, high chair
- Superhost/Excellent recent reviews, 4.8+ rating
- Flexible cancellation if your dates might change

What to read carefully in listings/reviews
- Recent guest photos and reviews mentioning noise, cleanliness, and accuracy of description
- Parking details and driveway size (important for SUVs/car seats)
- Any stairs or narrow entries if you have a stroller
- Host responsiveness (reviews will mention if they’re quick/helpful)
- House rules (no parties) — important during festivals

Sample message to send a host before booking
Hi — we’re a family of four (kids ages X and Y) planning to stay [dates]. Your place looks wonderful — can you confirm: 1) is there safe, on-site parking for one car, 2) do you provide a crib/pack ’n play and high chair (or can we rent one), and 3) are there any stairs or sharp drop-offs we should know about? Thanks!

Booking strategy
- If you’re visiting during a busy season (CMA Fest, holidays, big sporting events) book as early as possible.
- Prioritize listings with lots of recent reviews (last 6–12 months).
- If you’re driving, prioritize a place with a dedicated spot to avoid Uber surge or parking fines.
- Consider a short-term rental with self check-in if you’ll arrive late.

If you tell me dates, budget, and neighborhood preference (or must-haves), I can narrow this to 3–5 specific types of listings and draft messages you can copy/paste to hosts. Which dates and preferences should I use?
